question: Does the amount of Decode work that will remain alive while a new request enters Decode explain first-token compute queuing better than instantaneous concurrency?
source: same 34 cached A100 slow-placement physical points used by HIGH_LOAD_TTFT_DIAG_v1

signals.remaining_decode_tokens: sum(max(0, output_tokens-progress)) over already-active Decode requests at the target Prefill-to-Decode post-event boundary
signals.remaining_decode_profile_work_s: sum(remaining tokens multiplied by that request's current J0 profiled end-to-end Decode time)
signals.minimum_remaining_decode_tokens: minimum remaining tokens among active Decode competitors
signals.long_lived_competitor_count: count of active Decode competitors with at least eight remaining output tokens; eight is the fixed pipeline stage count, not a fitted threshold

outcome: reference first-Decode runtime minus J0/J1 predicted first-Decode profile duration
comparison: Pearson correlations and predeclared focus-pair safe-to-unsafe changes; no threshold fitting
